questions.q: Why does science keep changing our knowledge?
questions.a: New experiments and discoveries improve or replace old ideas, so science keeps evolving.

questions.q: Give one example of a scientific idea that changed over time.
questions.a: The idea that the sun moves around the earth was replaced by the earth orbiting the sun.

questions.q: What should we do when evidence contradicts a belief?
questions.a: Trust the evidence - test it, and change the belief if it holds.

questions.q: Why is questioning an answer part of science?
questions.a: Testing answers again and again checks them; a good answer survives every honest question.
A testable guess that explains an observation, checked by experiment.
By designing experiments whose results support one explanation over the other.

concepts.title: From Small Cells to Far Stars

questions.q: Name the smallest unit of life that science studies.
questions.a: The cell - all living things are made of cells.

questions.q: Name the largest structures science studies in the sky.
questions.a: Stars, galaxies and the universe beyond our solar system.

questions.q: What links cells and stars in one subject?
questions.a: Both are studied by science - the same habits of observation and testing explain tiny cells and far stars.

questions.q: What attitudes help in learning science this year?
questions.a: Curiosity, careful observation, honest recording and discussing ideas with others.

questions.q: How can you explore science outside the classroom?
questions.a: Watch plants, weather and stars, keep a nature diary, and try safe home experiments.

questions.q: Why is exploring joyful in science?
questions.a: Every question answered opens new wonders to discover.
